title: Reverse-transcriptase PCR
author: Cynthia L. Blanco
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tpsemne
materials: This protocol can be done at room temperature
RNA Isolation: Liver (quick guide to QIAGEN kit)
Do NOT use bleach around these reagents
Discard the flow-thorough, and repeat for remaining lysate
Replace collection tube with a clean one
RNA Isolation: Muscle (quick guide to QIAGEN kit)
Flash spin samples, then load into thermal cycler (Eppendorf, Thermostat, Hamburg, Germany).
Using the 5ng solution, prepare a 0.5ng stock:

steps.title: Prepare RNA Room and Glassware
steps.instruction: Clean the RNA room and prepare materials to ensure an RNase-free environment.

substeps.instruction: Change counter-top coverings.
Wipe all surfaces with RNAase-zap or an equivalent product.
Use RNAase-free plasticware.
Rinse all glassware with RNAase-zap.

steps.title: Prepare Buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare RLT and RPE buffers at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: If Buffer RLT has formed a precipitate, re-dissolve by gently warming, then return to room temperature.
In a fume hood, add 10 uL B-Mercaptoethanol (14.5M) per 1 mL RLT Buffer (prepared buffer can be stored for up to 1 month at room temperature).
Add 4 volumes of 100% ETOH to buffer RPE before first use.

steps.title: Extract RNA from Liver Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform RNA extraction using liver tissue samples at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Obtain 20 mg pieces of liver tissue and place into bead beater tubes (BioSpec Products, Inc., Oklahoma, USA) containing 0.7mm zirconia beads (fill tubes ~1/4 to ~1/3 full); keep on dry ice until ready.
Add 600 uL prepared RLT buffer to each tube and secure lids tightly.
Homogenize tissue in bead beater (Mini Beadbeater 16, BioSpec) for 1 minute, rest, then another minute.
Centrifuge samples for 3 minutes at full speed in the bead beater tube.
Remove 500 uL of supernatant into clean Eppendorf tubes, avoiding beads or debris; discard bead beater tubes.
Add 500 uL 50% ETOH to the cleared lysate and mix by pipetting.
Transfer up to 700 uL of sample to an RNeasy spin column placed inside a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add 700 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add another 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 10,000xg.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed.
Place spin column in a clean, labelled Eppendorf tube.
Add 50 uL RNase-free water to the spin column membrane without disturbing the membrane.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000xg.
Remove eluate from the collection tube, replace it into the spin column, and place the column back into the collection tube.
Centrifuge once more for 1 minute at 10,000xg.

steps.title: Extract RNA from Muscle Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform RNA extraction using muscle tissue samples at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Heat bead bath (Benchmark Iso-Block, Benchmark Scientific, New Jersey, USA) to 55°C.

Obtain 20 mg pieces of muscle tissue and place into bead beater (BioSpec Products, Inc., Oklahoma, USA) tubes containing 0.7mm zirconia beads (fill tubes ~1/4 to ~1/3 full); keep on dry ice until ready.
Add 300 uL prepared RLT buffer to each tube and secure lids tightly.
Homogenize tissue in bead beater (Mini Beadbeater 16, BioSpec) for 1 minute, rest, then another minute.
Add 590 uL RNase-free water and 10 uL Proteinase K to each tube, mix, and incubate at 55°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge samples for 3 minutes at full speed in the bead beater tube.
Remove 500 uL supernatant into clean Eppendorf tubes, avoiding beads or debris; discard bead beater tubes.
Add 250 uL of 100% ETOH to the cleared lysate and mix by pipetting.
Transfer up to 700 uL of sample to an RNeasy spin column placed inside a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add 350 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add another 350 uL buffer RW1 to the spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column and centrifuge for 15 seconds at 10,000xg.
Add another 500 uL buffer RPE to the spin column and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 10,000xg.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at full speed.
Place spin column in a clean, labelled Eppendorf tube.
Add 50 uL RNase-free water to the spin column membrane without disturbing the membrane.
Centrifuge for 1 minute at 10,000xg.
Remove eluate from the collection tube, replace it into the spin column, and place the column back into the collection tube.
Centrifuge once more for 1 minute at 10,000xg.

steps.title: Quantify and Evaluate RNA
steps.instruction: Determine RNA concentration and purity using spectrophotometry.

substeps.instruction: Quantify RNA via absorbance at 260 nm using an Epoch plate reader with Take3 microplate (BioTek, Vermont, USA).
Evaluate purity by calculating the ratio of absorbance at 260 nm divided by absorbance at 280 nm (BioTek).

steps.title: Prepare RNA Samples for cDNA Synthesis
steps.instruction: Dilute RNA samples on wet ice using PCR-clean plasticware.

substeps.instruction: Dilute RNA samples to a total volume of 1ug RNA in 10uL RNAase free H2O.
Dilute each sample in triplicate to create 3 batches of cDNA per sample.
Select one sample for the standard curve and prepare an additional set of triplicates for it.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA
steps.instruction: Perform reverse transcription using the High Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Life Technologies, California, USA).

substeps.instruction: Calculate the total number of reactions (3 per sample) and add extra reactions to account for pipetting loss.
Prepare the Master Mix.
Add 10 uL of master mix into tubes containing 10 uL diluted RNA and mix by pipetting.
Run cDNA reactions.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Plate
steps.instruction: Set up the RT-PCR plate using TaqMan (Applied Biosystems, California, USA) master mix.

substeps.instruction: Calculate total reactions (2 per cDNA sample) and add extra for pipetting loss.
Combine ingredients in a separate tube to make the master mix.
Pipette 19 uL of master mix into each sample well and standard curve wells (excluding the first two wells of the standard curve).
Pipette 1 uL cDNA into each sample well in duplicate and mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Curve and Controls
steps.instruction: Set up the standard curve in duplicate and include no-template controls (NTC).

substeps.instruction: Load the first two wells of the standard curve with 100ng RNA.
Load the next two wells with 50ng RNA.
Create a 1:10 dilution from the 50ng stock (1ul of 50ng into 9ul of H2O) and load 1 uL into the next two wells (5ng).
Create a 1:10 dilution from the 5ng stock (1ul of 5ng into 9ul of H2O) and load 1 uL into the next two wells (0.5ng).
Load 1 uL RNAase free H2O into the last wells as no template controls (NTC).

steps.title: Run RT-PCR
steps.instruction: Execute the PCR reactions using the RT-PCR instrument (Applied Biosystems, California, USA).

substeps.instruction: Seal the plate with a sticker and centrifuge briefly on a plate spinner.
Load the plate into the instrument.
Perform PCR reactions: Repeat the specified steps 3 and 4 for 40 cycles.
Set the detector: Highlight sample wells and select the appropriate detector.
Label NTC wells as 'NTC', standard curve wells as 'Standard' (indicating RNA amount), and other wells as 'Unknown' (labeling samples but not quantities).

steps.title: Analyze RT-PCR Data
steps.instruction: Process the output data to determine normalized RNA content.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the threshold is in the logarithmic portion of the graph and matches thresholds for the same detector (within 0.2-0.3 units for normalization).
Verify the slope of the graph is approximately -3.3 ± 10% (reflecting 100% ± 10% efficiency).
Obtain the starting quantity of RNA for each well from the program output.
Average the replicates for each sample.
Divide the sample average of the target gene by the corresponding sample average of the housekeeping gene control to get normalized RNA content.
Calculate the mean and standard error for each treatment group.
Calculate fold change from control to treatment using the provided equation.
